conceptual.anchor: Four epistemic statuses ... Candidate \rightarrow Supported \rightarrow Accepted \rightarrow Committed ... Supported \rightarrow Contested ... Supported \rightarrow Rejected ... Candidate \rightarrow Unresolved ... These are not simply levels of "confidence." They represent different domain states.

formal.anchor: Formal acceptance function ... \alpha_\rho: EA\times P\times C \rightarrow \mathcal S_A ... \mathcal S_A=\{Candidate,Supported,Accepted,Rejected,Contested,Unresolved\} ... an assertion can be Supported + Contested. So again, we should be careful about a single enum.

governance.anchor: Acceptance policy ... \rho_A = AcceptancePolicy ... Evidence requirements N_{independent}\geq2 ... Source requirements Authority(Source)\geq A_{min} ... Temporal requirements Age(e)\leq T_{max} ... Conflict requirements ActiveConflict(P)=False ... Human approval ... Statistical threshold Pr(P\mid E)

lexical.anchor:
The central distinction is: Supported 
eq Accepted 
eq Committed 
eq True. This distinction should become one of the core laws of KnowledgeOS.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The problem ... Strong supporting evidence, No known contradiction, Current, High provenance quality ... Can KnowledgeOS now put P into the Knowledge State as accepted knowledge? Not necessarily. There is a missing concept: AcceptancePolicy. The evidence tells us what the evidence supports. The acce
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues even strong, uncontradicted, current, high-provenance evidence does not automatically warrant acceptance, introducing AcceptancePolicy as the missing concept determining what may be admitted as accepted knowledge.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Commitment is purpose-dependent ... Commit_\rho(P,Purpose,Authority) ... Commit(P,migration,ArchitectureBoard) may require more than Commit(P,internal research,Engineer). Commit(P,P_1)\neq Commit(P,P_2). This fits our earlier Ideal State principle: I_t(P_1)\neq I_t(P_2).
rationale_evidence.statement: Defines Commit_ρ(P,Purpose,Authority) as purpose-dependent, e.g. migration commitment requiring Architecture Board authority versus lighter requirements for internal research, echoing the earlier purpose-dependence of the Ideal State.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Why "Accepted + Contested" is possible ... an architecture board has formally accepted ... another architect disputes ... Accepted(P)=True while Contested(P)=True. This is not logically impossible. ... The proposition is institutionally accepted while still being epistemically contested. This is exa
rationale_evidence.statement: Justifies Accepted+Contested coexisting via an architecture-board example (formally accepted decision still disputed by an architect), establishing that epistemic status and governance status must not be collapsed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Acceptance and Ideal State ... MustBeVerified(BackupStatus) ... Supported(P) may still fail the ideal requirement: \Sigma_K(P)\not\models I^K(P). Accepted(P) \not\Rightarrow IdealSatisfied(P). A proposition can be accepted while the knowledge objective remains incomplete.
rationale_evidence.statement: Connects Acceptance to the Ideal State: Accepted(P) ⇏ IdealSatisfied(P) — a proposition can be accepted while the underlying knowledge objective (e.g. independent verification) remains incomplete.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The acceptance lattice question ... Candidate, Supported, Accepted, Committed look like a ladder, but they are not universally ordered. Accepted\not\Rightarrow Committed. Contested can coexist with Accepted. AcceptanceStatus should be modeled as a state space, not a scalar hierarchy.
rationale_evidence.statement: Corrects the apparent ladder Candidate→Supported→Accepted→Committed: it is not a universal ordering (Accepted⇏Committed; Contested can coexist with Accepted), so AcceptanceStatus must be a state space, not a scalar hierarchy.

## Rationale
Argues even strong, uncontradicted, current, high-provenance evidence does not automatically warrant acceptance, introducing AcceptancePolicy as the missing concept determining what may be admitted as accepted knowledge [S0863]. Defines Commit_ρ(P,Purpose,Authority) as purpose-dependent, e.g. migration commitment requiring Architecture Board authority versus lighter requirements for internal research, echoing the earlier purpose-dependence of the Ideal State [S0863]. Justifies Accepted+Contested coexisting via an architecture-board example (formally accepted decision still disputed by an architect), establishing that epistemic status and governance status must not be collapsed [S0863]. Connects Acceptance to the Ideal State: Accepted(P) ⇏ IdealSatisfied(P) — a proposition can be accepted while the underlying knowledge objective (e.g. independent verification) remains incomplete [S0863]. Corrects the apparent ladder Candidate→Supported→Accepted→Committed: it is not a universal ordering (Accepted⇏Committed; Contested can coexist with Accepted), so AcceptanceStatus must be a state space, not a scalar hierarchy [S0863].
